# Assembled continuation and Live controls

`make linux-application-test` owns the native application comparison and existing command/settings component check. Both `make linux-command-test` and `make linux-continuation-test` depend on it; requesting both executes the shared run once. The runner prepares native PCM/Codex/input/cleanup executables before entering private X11/Openbox, HOME/XDG state, session/accessibility buses, network/PID namespaces, masked system bus and devices, and software Mesa. It needs the documented desktop runner prerequisites and ImageMagick; no Python environment or interpreter is needed.

[The independent reference](released-application-continuation.json), SHA-256 `6eb14b0df7438157ef4546db2bf6b9a51a84b130d0073b2f8f4520adc703e942`, contains 28 states, two layouts, seven speech requests, two complete Codex turns and three distinct source revisions. The 4,025-line/118,346-byte document comes from untouched v1.6.0 at `5202477edfe4b5d8bacfa5b2e9fd6eadd9624f7f`. The temporary observer checks every released application module against that commit before activation and verifies imported paths/digests afterward. It invokes the actual application, public actions, GTK controls, clipboard and compatible stores; no handler or service owner is replaced. Synthetic PCM/Codex executables and a loopback speech endpoint supply only external inputs. Collectors remain under ignored `tmp/` and are absent from native execution.

At this continuation checkpoint, the shared application harness reached ten workflows/100 states. The subsequent [Live workspace extension](live-workspace-evidence.md) brings it to eleven workflows/122 states. The original eight-workflow, command and continuation fixtures remain byte-for-byte unchanged. Shared assembly, shutdown, process reaping, GTK traversal, settling and window capture replace duplicated setup. There is no new production API for tests.

The retired `linux/tests/continuation_controls_smoke.py` was introduced with continuation/rewrite controls in `4bcf12a` and strengthened by `1c2609f` and subsequent Live/cancellation changes. Its executable owner was the Make target. At this checkpoint, two microphone/speech stand-ins moved unchanged into their remaining consumer, `screenshot_workspace_smoke.py`; the later [native image comparison](application-images-evidence.md) retires that consumer too. The 330-line obsolete continuation script and its preview/handler/delivery mocks are removed, with these contracts retained:

| Contract | Native observation |
| --- | --- |
| Edited originals and rewrites survive append | Real editor changes, Continue, preparation, recording, Stop and durable parent/reply text |
| Parent text stays visible during recognition and final reconciliation | Every nonempty source-buffer revision, plus real three-second PCM batch preview and final speech |
| Widget preview and copy-only guidance | Actual private D-Bus messages through the public status action, including preparation, recording, processing and the complete continued preview |
| Final combined text copies without early segment delivery | Private clipboard at each observed stage, actual speech requests and saved results |
| Grouped History and immutable raw recordings | Actual row text, recording count, source/reply stores and expanded Original recordings |
| History Copy and child-to-parent focus | Click the real Current text Copy button; focus a saved segment and observe its parent |
| Once consumes itself after finalization | Actual Live control, provider preview/final turns, final reply and current/persisted preferences |
| Continuous survives cancellation; Off disables it | Actual control cycle, recorder cancellation, unchanged History and persisted settings |
| Model/effort save, reset and failure recovery | Real model catalog, public combo choices, durable configuration and rollback after a private config-path failure |
| Wide/minimum controls fit | Exact released bounds, visibility and sensitivity for Continue, Live and Record, plus full X11 captures |
| Repeated widget Continue targets the requested note | Real registered review action while another conversation is displayed; two append/copy/store cycles |
| Preparation cancellation and silent append preserve the note | Real capture cancellation and an empty HTTP transcription, without extra durable entries |
| An unrelated recording starts fresh | Record button after continuation, new live source and cancellation |

The separate [Live/capture comparison](live-evidence.md) retains realtime transport, immediate notification, manual revisions, delayed providers and final coalescing; this new application owner adds root settings, archive, review-action and service wiring. `linux-live-stability-test` and `linux-fluid-workspace-test` remain separate Python owners for their remaining motion, diagram and interaction contracts. This conversion does not silently retire them.

The new comparison exposed a production ordering bug. Native capture assigned the parent's fallback title before the application's archive refresh, so its nested original-recording label became `First raw`; the released label remained `First.` while only the outer conversation title changed. `tmp/native-continuation-before-fix.log` fails specifically on those nested row titles after generated timestamps are normalized. Capture now completes the archive refresh before enqueueing title work. The same independent observations pass after that owner repair; no expected title was changed to native output.

Generated entry IDs and the full generated date/time are normalized. User text, History grouping/outcomes, public controls and provider prompts remain exact. Uploaded WAVs are compared by byte length and SHA-256, including both preview and final audio. Empty buffer notifications and consecutive duplicate source revisions are omitted; any different nonempty intermediate source remains observable. The existing fixed-input [History page comparison](history-page-evidence.md) separately owns date formatting in its recorded `Europe/Prague` timezone.

The released reference uses GTK 4.22.4/Pango 1.58.2, disabled animations/cursor blink, UTC and software rendering. Requested window sizes are 1060×780 and 420×520; client bounds are 1050×770 and 410×510. Both continuation observers park only the isolated pointer outside the window before capture. That removes an incidental hover from the native harness's earlier workflows without changing application styling or the command capture contract. Both continuation images and all four retained command images have zero differing pixels in `tmp/native-continuation-pixel-comparison.log`.

Actual Make fails at a positively verified interpreter trap before conversion (`tmp/native-continuation-before-make.log`) and passes both requested targets with Python/uv blocked afterward (`tmp/native-continuation-accepted-make.log`). Final application evidence is `tmp/application/run.jic3Ut/session.gGxyhS/`; the independent reference is `tmp/native-continuation-reference-dates-evidence/session.jPMJAz/released-continuation-x1i26cgi/`. Shutdown acknowledges platform closure, reaps recorded PCM/provider children and removes ephemeral Codex workspaces. Speech request count/audio and both complete preview/final inputs, model and effort match.

Adjacent capture verification passes 46 transactions/218 released states and three native exit/privacy faults; Live verification passes 26 transactions/122 states; capture controls and conversation/scrolling also pass (`tmp/native-continuation-siblings-final.log`). The archive check initially inherited UTC from that scratch runner; its only differences were the expected two-hour display offset. With the reference timezone it passes nine pages/64 states (`tmp/native-continuation-history.log`). The retained screenshot consumer passes its five ownership/context/privacy assertions (`tmp/native-continuation-screenshot.log`).

The final full gate passes 139 native tests, zero failures and 68 explicitly ignored environment checks across 98 suites, both strict Clippy configurations, formatting, generated consistency, ShellCheck and diff checks. The remaining Python gate passes 571 tests and Ruff/formatting for 158 files, retaining its existing PyGObject deprecation warning. Logs are `tmp/native-continuation-final-native.log`, `tmp/native-continuation-final-python.log` and `tmp/native-continuation-final-gates-evidence/session.eOOzyJ/`. No hosted runner is used.

The first full run failed in unchanged `mluva-core` terminal support while observing a synthetic process's executable switch (`tmp/native-continuation-native-initial-failure.log`). Its standalone replay and complete-gate replay pass without changes to that subsystem (`tmp/native-continuation-terminal-recheck.log`). The intermittent fixture failure remains a follow-up if it recurs; it is not presented as a repaired production delivery bug.

Final review keeps the unchanged earlier fixtures, active screenshot consumer and distinct Live/motion owners. Production changes add ten lines and remove seven; Make adds five and removes nine. Test/support adds 606 lines and removes 398, including the retired 330-line script and consolidated setup; the independent 4,025-line fixture and documentation are separate. The extra native observation records real clipboard, provider, archive and lifecycle effects instead of reproducing application callbacks.

Both implementations emit the same pre-existing narrow GtkText allocation warning. The released collector also emits its GdkX11 deprecation warning; the private display's teardown message is expected. These checks prove the recorded isolated X11 application paths, not real compositor/physical keys, microphone or provider accounts, complete Live/image/Meeting flows, every theme/scale, clean-distribution dependencies, complete Python removal or runtime performance. Every complete-workflow parity row remains Pending. The protected installed app/widget remain 1.6.0.
